restated: Let f(q,r) be defined by the Brouwer recurrence (MISSION section 2), so that for q>=r>=0 f(q,r) is the unique p>r with either r<p<q and [p,p,r] a P-position of 3-row Chomp, or p>=q and [p,q,r] a P-position. Call row r stale if only finitely many P-positions [p,q,r] with p>=q>=r exist, and for a stale row let N(r) be 1 + the largest such q. Then for every stale row r: with q0 the least q>=r such that f(q,r)<=q, one has f(q0,r)=q0, f(q,r)=q0 for all q>=q0, N(r)=q0+1, and q0<=2r+1. Hence N(r)<=2r+2 for every stale row, and N(r)<=3r for every stale row r>=1.
ledger_statement: N(r) <= 2r+2 for every STALE row r (a row with finitely many P-positions), hence N(r) <= 3r for r >= 1, closing (B1) of byrnes_audit.md with K(r)=2r+2. Let q0 be the least q>=r with f(q,r)<=q. (1) f(q0,r)=q0: if p=f(q0,r)<q0 then by Sheiner Lemma 2.1 r<p<q0 and [p,p,r] is P, so f(p,r)=p, contradicting minimality of q0. So the row is constant with value c_r=q0, its last P-position [p,q,r] (p>=q) is at q=q0, and N(r)=c_r+1. (2) c_r<=2r+1: if c_r>r+1, Sheiner Lemma 4.2 (row-start propagation, Lean-verified) at q=r+1 gives b<r with f(r+1,b)=c_r, and #G07 s8.1 (=C0012) gives f(r+1,b) <= (r+1)+b+1 <= 2r+1. Replaces the earlier route via #G07 s8.8 and 'A029902 is increasing', which is unproved (constant-row values increasing in r).
